title: finding(data-objectstack): `exportDownload`'s error ladder cannot read the REST flat dialect — a 403 that names the missing grant reaches the operator as the word "Forbidden" (34 codes affected)
body:
## Observation

Found from a HotCRM report: a console operator clicks **导出为 CSV** on the `crm_lead` list
view and the toolbar reports one word — `Forbidden`. No code, no object, no hint at what to
grant. Screenshot-level symptom; the server was in fact answering something useful.

`exportDownload` in `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:4627` reads its failure like this
(L4679–L4682):

```ts
const res = await this.fetchImpl(url, { method: 'GET', headers, credentials: 'include' });
if (!res.ok) {
  const errorBody = await res.json().catch(() => ({ message: res.statusText }));
  const err = new Error(errorBody?.error?.message || errorBody?.message || res.statusText) as any;
  err.status = res.status;
  throw err;
}
```

That ladder reads two envelope shapes: ADR-0112 nested (`error: { message }`) and flat-with-
`message`. `packages/rest`'s export gate writes neither.

## Measured

Live dev server, `@objectstack/{console,rest,plugin-security,spec}` all `17.4.0`,
`GET /api/v1/data/crm_lead/export?format=csv&limit=1`:

```
HTTP 403
{"code":"EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED","error":"Export is not permitted on object 'crm_lead' for this user","object":"crm_lead"}
```

`error` is a **string**, and there is no `message` key. So `errorBody?.error?.message` is
`undefined`, `errorBody?.message` is `undefined`, and the ladder falls through to
`res.statusText`.

Running the ladder verbatim over three bodies measured on that same server:

| body | source | ladder yields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{code:'EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED', error:'Export is not permitted on object …', object:'crm_lead'}` | 403, `enforceExportPermission` | **`"Forbidden"`** |
| `{error:'UNAUTHENTICATED', code:'UNAUTHENTICATED', message:'Authentication is required to access this endpoint.'}` | 401, **same URL** | `"Authentication is required to access this endpoint."` |
| `{success:false, error:{code:'ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND', message:'Not found'}}` | 404, ADR-0112 nested | `"Not found"` |

The middle row is the control that makes this a reader defect rather than a producer one:
**the same URL, the same ladder, one status apart** — 401 renders a sentence, 403 renders the
HTTP status word. The one body the ladder cannot read is the one carrying the actionable
sentence, because it is the only one of the three with no `message` key.

Producer, for reference — `@objectstack/rest` `enforceExportPermission`:

```js
res.status(403).json({
  code: "EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED",
  error: `Export is not permitted on object '${objectName}' for this user`,
  object: objectName
});
```

## Blast radius

Not one route. Scanning the shipped `@objectstack/rest@17.4.0` bundle for `.json({…})` bodies
that carry both `code` and `error` but no `message` yields **34 distinct error codes** in the
ladder's blind spot, including the ones an operator is most likely to hit:

```
ALREADY_REVERTED · ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED · APPROVAL_ACTIONS_FAILED · APPROVAL_RECALL_FAILED
APPROVAL_REQUEST_GET_FAILED · APPROVAL_REQUEST_LIST_FAILED · BATCH_NOT_ATOMIC · BATCH_TOO_LARGE
EMAIL_SEND_FAILED · EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED · FORM_NOT_FOUND · FORM_RESOLVE_FAILED
IMPORT_JOB_CREATE_FAILED · INVALID_FILTER · INVALID_REQUEST · LOOKUP_NOT_PUBLIC
LOOKUP_TARGET_MISSING · NOT_FOUND · NOT_IMPLEMENTED · NOT_UNDOABLE · PERMISSION_DENIED
REPORTS_LIST_FAILED · REPORT_DELETE_FAILED · REPORT_GET_FAILED · REPORT_NOT_FOUND
REPORT_RUN_FAILED · REPORT_SAVE_FAILED · REPORT_SCHEDULE_FAILED · REQUEST_NOT_FOUND
RULE_NOT_FOUND · SCHEDULES_LIST_FAILED · SCHEDULE_DELETE_FAILED · VALIDATION_ERROR
VALIDATION_FAILED
```

`VALIDATION_ERROR` / `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `INVALID_FILTER` / `PERMISSION_DENIED` reaching a
user as `"Bad Request"` / `"Forbidden"` is the same loss with a much wider audience than the
export button.

The identical ladder is copied at five more sites in this one module — L3376–L3378, L4593–L4594,
L4679–L4680, L4902–L4903, and the `response.statusText` pair at L6551 / L6609 — so whatever is
decided here wants to land once, not six times.

## Why this is the reader's card and not the producer's

The flat dialect is **not** a producer bug to file: objectstack#9559 is the live ratchet owner
for `packages/rest`'s flat dialect, it explicitly holds down the `stringError 44` debt left
behind by objectstack#7035 / PR #7293, it is marked "tracking card, not a work card", and
ADR-0112 D5 leaves the flat shape's permanent position an **open** maintainer question. So the
flat body is on the wire today, is known, is owned, and may legitimately stay.

Which means the reader has to tolerate it while it is there. Right now it does not, and it
fails in the direction that costs the most — it discards a sentence naming the exact grant to
add and substitutes a word that names nothing.

Same family, different modules, each of which got its own card rather than a rider:
objectui#7959 (`fetchPackages` opens no body at all), objectui#7938 (`fetchFullPackage` drops
`error.userMessage`), objectui#7368 (the report channel). This is that family's
`data-objectstack` member, and it is a **structural** miss rather than a dropped optional
field: no key the ladder looks for exists in the body.

## Worth deciding

1. **Extend the ladder one rung** — `error?.message` → `message` → **`typeof error === 'string' ? error : undefined`** → `statusText`. Smallest change, reads every shape on the wire today, and needs no producer change. Optionally append `code` when present, so an operator can search for `EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED`.
2. **Extract one shared envelope reader** in `data-objectstack` and route all six sites through it, with a pin. Fixes the drift the six copies invite, which is the shape that produced this card — and is the same option 2 objectui#7959 raised for `app-shell`. If both land, a single reader shared across packages is the honest end state.
3. **Leave it and record why** — e.g. if the ruling is that the flat dialect must die first (objectstack#9559 reaching zero) and readers should not grow tolerance for a shape slated for removal. Defensible, but it should be the recorded answer rather than the default, and it leaves 34 codes rendering as status words until that card closes — a card that by its own rules is not dispatchable as a unit.

## Re-check

```bash
# the ladder
sed -n '4627,4685p' packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts
grep -n "error?.message || .*?.message || .*statusText" packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts

# the producer body, against any running server where the caller lacks allowExport
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $KEY" "http://localhost:4001/api/v1/data/crm_lead/export?format=csv&limit=1"
# → {"code":"EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED","error":"Export is not permitted …","object":"crm_lead"}

# the control, same URL, no credential
curl -s "http://localhost:4001/api/v1/data/crm_lead/export?format=csv&limit=1"
# → {"error":"UNAUTHENTICATED","code":"UNAUTHENTICATED","message":"Authentication is required …"}
```

## Not in scope

Whether the caller *should* have been denied. It should have been: objectstack#8681's maintainer
ruling (2026-08-15) deliberately removed `allowExport` from the org-admin wildcard, and the
denial here is that ruling working as designed. The defect is only that the console makes the
ruling unreadable — the operator is told `Forbidden` when the server said which object, which
user, and which axis.

Related: objectstack#9559 (producer-side ratchet owner) · objectstack#8681 / #3544 (why the 403
is correct) · objectui#7959 / #7938 / #7368 (same reader family) · ADR-0112 D5.
